extracted.intended_audience: general public interested in culture/entertainment news
extracted.subtask_description: A news report about a comedian's homophobic stand-up routine and subsequent public apology, including reactions from advocacy groups, audience members, and venue organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid advocating violence or threats in comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Morgan said he would 'pull out a knife and stab' his son if the son came out as gay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks that depict or endorse violence (even framed as a joke) are identified as beyond acceptable comedic boundaries; the article states such content 'went too far' and was 'not funny in any context.' Comedians should avoid violent threats as punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology sufficiency — must make amends beyond words
rubrics_metrics.description: Bloggers and others are already questioning whether Morgan's apology is sufficient. The Human Rights Campaign's Fred Sainz: 'he did the right thing by apologizing, but that's just not enough... he now has a responsibility to make amends.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An apology from a public figure should include corrective actions and concrete amends, not just words; audiences and advocacy groups may expect further steps to repair harm and 'correct the record.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public figures' responsibility as role models
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He's a role model and Morgan now has a responsibility to make amends for his horribly hurtful and dangerous "comedy" routine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers with public influence are held to higher standards; their comedic choices carry responsibility because they can affect public attitudes and vulnerable groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting minorities — 'punching down' is unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience member Kevin Rogers: 'For one minority to attack another minority in such a way, without provocation, is appalling and in no way humorous.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes that single out or attack marginalized groups (including intra-minority attacks) are likely to be judged harmful and not funny. Comedians should avoid material that punches down or denigrates vulnerable communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context does not automatically excuse hateful remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Morgan acknowledged that 'even in a comedy club' what he said went too far 'and was not funny in any context.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers cannot reliably use 'it was just a joke' or venue context to excuse language that advocates harm or expresses hate; the acceptability of a joke should be evaluated on its content and impact, not solely its setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience expectations and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I went to Tracy Morgan's show to laugh and enjoy someone who I thought was a brilliant comic... I left feeling like the joke was on me,' said an audience member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences expect to be entertained, not to be targeted or harmed. Breaching that trust by delivering hateful or violent material can alienate attendees and damage a comedian's relationship with their audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dismiss victims or minimize bullying
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the remarks attributed to Morgan: Being gay is a choice and young victims of bullying directed at gays are simply 'whining.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy that mocks victims or minimizes their experiences (e.g., bullying) is likely to be perceived as poor judgment and insensitive; such framing undermines the moral acceptability of the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue and organizer accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ryman Auditorium issued its own apology afterward for Morgan's behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues may be expected to respond to problematic performances with public statements or remedial actions; organizers share responsibility for events held on their stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media and public scrutiny as mechanisms of accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Bloggers and others are already questioning whether Morgan's apology is sufficient; material was highlighted in various published reports quoting audience members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage by media, blogs, and eyewitness accounts functions to evaluate and call out problematic comedy, increasing pressure on performers and institutions to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor that reinforces harmful stereotypes has dangerous consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Fred Sainz called the routine 'horribly hurtful and dangerous "comedy" routine,' warning that no one should 'become a victim of violence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes that perpetuate prejudice or normalize violence against marginalized groups can contribute to real-world harm; creators should consider potential social consequences when crafting material.
